blocks.md: Welcome to **Conclusion** (Vol II). This overview gives you the chapter's big ideas before the section-by-section lessons. Read the claims once, flip the flashcards, then take the warm-up quiz: it is fine to miss questions here, the lessons that follow fill the gaps.

Machine learning at fleet scale is judged by the whole system, and a local improvement can move cost into a layer that its designer did not measure. Faster computation can expose a network bottleneck; larger jobs can lose more work to failure; a service that meets latency targets can still lack evidence required for deployment. The model remains central, but its accuracy and execution speed do not determine whether the complete system delivers useful work.
